channel.title: Said & Checked: Education — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day about Education, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, Education, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Thomas Massie)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Thomas Massie, U.S. Representative: “We saw the president of Harvard University resign in the face of these revelations.” Unsettled. No source read reports a sitting Harvard president resigning; AP reported on Feb. 25, 2026 that former president Larry Summers would retire from his Harvard teaching posts during the university's review of his Epstein ties. The statement fits only if it refers to a former president.

item.title: Said & Checked, Education, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Donald Trump)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “Since its inception in 1979, the Department of Education has managed to waste over 3 trillion taxpayer dollars without directly educating students or improving their academic performance.” Unsettled. No Department of Education spending series since 1979 could be read (the ed.gov budget history page refused the request), so the $3 trillion total was not checked. Whether the spending was waste that produced no direct education is a judgment that no dataset settles.
  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “National assessments in recent years reveal alarming trends, with mathematics and reading scores plummeting” Unsettled. AskAmerica's NAEP data show 2024 national scores below 2019 in all four grade-subject series (grade 8 math 281.0 to 272.2; grade 4 reading 219.4 to 214.3). Against 2022, grade 4 math rose (234.9 to 237.3) and grade 8 math was nearly flat (273.1 to 272.2) while both reading series fell, so whether scores are 'plummeting' depends on the baseline year.

item.title: Said & Checked, Education, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Sarah Huckabee Sanders)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Sarah Huckabee Sanders, Governor of Arkansas: “we made sure that our public schools had the largest investment in state history. We paid our teachers better. We opened up paid maternity leave, one of only two states in the country to do that for up to 12…” Unsettled. The only source read for these claims is the governor's own office, which says a 2023 law raised starting teacher pay from $36,000 to $50,000 and gave teachers up to 12 weeks of paid maternity leave, and which cites a teacher-policy group for the two-state count. That group's report page loaded without the figure, and no budget record on school funding was read.
  • Sarah Huckabee Sanders, Governor of Arkansas: “We opened a Merit Incentive Fund where we have given $50 million in bonuses to our teachers over the course of the last 3.5 years.” Unsettled. The only source read is the governor's own office, whose June 2026 release says the fund has awarded "more than $50 million in merit pay for over 12,000 educators" over three years. The state education department's page with the award totals could not be loaded, so no independent total was read.
